audit.why: Packet win rate is 41.7 over 940 games — by far the largest sample in this slice and the only one worth leaning on. HARD at 8/10 matches it.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer never names Zaahen's ultimate at all — it literally uses the placeholder word 'Ultimate' in winCon, enemyWin, breakdown.wave, breakdown.cooldowns, breakdown.feeding, breakdown.trading, loading, dosFull, dontsFull, tradeBad, focus.text and five report entries.
audit.why: The ability is Grim Deliverance. Every one of those strings reads as unfinished generation output, and 'is Ultimate down?' is not information — it is a template that never got filled. This is the single most visible defect in the matchup.
audit.corrected: Replaced 'Ultimate' with the real name, or with the ability that actually matters in that sentence, everywhere the length band allowed. focus.text still reads 'Zaahen Ultimate' and needs a hand edit — see notes.

audit.whatIsWrong: Dreaded Return is never mentioned anywhere in either layer. Both layers instead describe Zaahen as 'walking you down'.
audit.why: Dreaded Return is an 850-range stab that pulls everything it hits toward him. Against a 550-range immobile mage that is the entire matchup — he does not need to close the gap on foot, he reaches out and takes her. Mel's Radiant Volley is 950 and Solar Snare 1000, so his pull threatens from barely inside her own poke range, on a 14-second cooldown. Telling the player to 'give up wave position rather than health once his gap-close is online' points her at the dash while the pull is what actually kills her.
audit.corrected: Named Dreaded Return and its 850 range and 14s cooldown in tldr, enemyWin, phases[3].why, breakdown.cooldowns, loading, tradeBad, report[5].t, content.early, content.mid, wants.foe[0], whys[2] and whys[3].

audit.whatIsWrong: Cultivation of War is never mentioned, and Mel's entire win condition here is 'stack Overwhelm and execute'.
audit.why: When Determination fills, Zaahen gains bonus attack damage and can revive. Mel's whole plan is an execute — a threshold kill that the passive can simply refund. A player who does not know a revive exists will burn Golden Eclipse on a kill that undoes itself and then have no ultimate for the fight that follows. This is the most important thing in his kit for a champion whose payoff is an execute, and it was absent.
audit.corrected: Stated the revive in spikes[2].text, content.late and whys[6].

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[4] tells the player her 'W Rebuttal reflect can flip a careless engage', and phases[1].why says the reflect turns his poke into hers.
audit.why: Zaahen has no projectile on any slot — The Darkin Glaive is an empowered attack, Dreaded Return a stab-and-pull, Aureate Rush a dash and Grim Deliverance a downward stab. Rebuttal has nothing to send back, so its value here is the damage prevention alone. This is the third matchup in this slice where the reflect is being sold against a kit that owns nothing reflectable.
audit.corrected: Rewrote whys[4] and phases[1].why as damage immunity spent on Grim Deliverance.
sources: champ-data/_kits/zaahen.json (no projectile flag on any slot)

audit.whatIsWrong: Itemization names Blackfire Torch, Shadowflame, Rabadon's and Zhonya's and no anti-heal, in a matchup the content layer itself calls a sustain loss ('extended trades his sustain wins', 'his durability and sustain out-scale your poke').
audit.why: The Darkin Glaive heals him on the empowered attack and Grim Deliverance heals for a portion of the damage it deals. The file diagnoses the sustain problem in three separate strings and then never prescribes Grievous Wounds. Morellonomicon is the fix and it belongs in the build, not in a vague 'you cannot chip him down anymore'.
audit.corrected: Put Morellonomicon into report[8].t, content.mid, whys[5] and loading.
sources: champ-data/_kits/zaahen.json (heal flag on Q and R)

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contains no numbers, and tradeBad, dontsFull[2].d and breakdown.trading claim Rebuttal is 'gone for twenty seconds'.
audit.why: Rebuttal is 38/35/33/29/26, so 38 seconds at lane rank. Grim Deliverance is 110/95/80, Dreaded Return 14/13.5/13/12.5/12 and Aureate Rush 10/9.5/9/8.5/8. The gap between a 14-second pull and a 38-second Rebuttal is the reason this matchup sits at 41.7 percent, and neither number appeared anywhere.
audit.corrected: Filled breakdown.cooldowns with the real figures and corrected the Rebuttal number wherever it appeared.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Darkin Glaive's auto-attack reset and its recast knockup are never mentioned.
audit.why: The Darkin Glaive empowers his next attack and can be recast so the following attack knocks up. That means his burst opens on an attack wind-up rather than a visible ability cast, and there is a second knockup queued behind the first hit. For an immobile mage the tell she should be watching is the attack animation, not a spell effect.
audit.corrected: Named the recast knockup and the heal on The Darkin Glaive in wants.foe[1], whys[5] and the itemization line.
sources: champ-data/_kits/zaahen.json (Q autoReset and knockup flags, recast described in Riot text)

audit.whatIsWrong: content.spikes has 3 entries where every other matchup in the file has 4. The packet flags this directly.
audit.why: The renderer expects four spike rows, and the three present are the thinnest strings in the whole Mel file — 'Free poke window before his gap-close comes online' is 49 characters carrying no ability name, no number and no instruction.
audit.corrected: Rewrote all three in place to carry real ability names. A fourth entry cannot be proposed as a before/after edit because there is no existing string to match against — suggested text for spikes[3] is in notes.

notes: TWO THINGS NEED A HAND EDIT. (1) focus.text still reads 'Zaahen Ultimate'. The real name is Grim Deliverance, but 'Zaahen Grim Deliverance' is 23 characters against a 15-character original and cannot pass the +/-10% band. Honestly the better focus for this matchup is not the ultimate at all — it is Dreaded Return, the 850-range pull, which is what actually kills an immobile 550-range mage. Suggested: focus.text = 'Zaahen Dreaded Return', focus.letters = ['W']. (2) content.spikes has only 3 entries where every other Mel matchup has 4, and the packet flags it. I cannot propose a fourth as a before/after edit since there is no string on disk to match. Suggested spikes[3] = { when: 'Full Determination', text: 'His passive can revive him — the execute may not stick' }. THE PLACEHOLDER BUG: the full layer used the literal word 'Ultimate' as an ability name in eighteen places. That reads as unfinished generation output rather than content, and it is worth grepping the whole repo for other matchups where an ability name never got substituted. DID NOT ASSERT: _missing-interactions.json claims 'Your Rebuttal (W) shuts off Zaahen's Aureate Rush (E) — hold it for the engage'. That comes from a 'terrain' flag on Rebuttal which is derived, not stated — Riot's own text for Rebuttal describes a barrier that reflects projectiles, prevents damage and grants move speed, with no terrain at all. Whether Rebuttal physically blocks a dash is unverified, so I built none of this matchup's advice on it. If someone confirms it on the Wiki it is a significant upgrade to the level 6 plan. THIRD MATCHUP IN THIS SLICE where the file sells Rebuttal's reflect against a kit with no projectile (see also mel/wukong, mel/yone, mel/warwick) — worth a sweep of the whole Mel file.
